quote.text: … you must never forget that every one of these figures comes in the first instance from the village watchman, who just puts down what he damn pleases.
quote.author: Widely attributed to Sir Josiah Stamp (1880–1941). The attribution is contested — which, this issue, is rather the point.

macro.title: What It Means For VWRA, Global Bonds, Gold And Bitcoin

reads.label: Gold’s $109 fall was arithmetic, not sentiment
reads.text: — real yields up, dollar up, risk assets down too. Bitcoin is the same factor with more beta.

stories.kicker: The World · France and the Guard
stories.headline: France names an IRGC cyber unit for sabotaging 700 supermarkets’ fridges
stories.dek: Paris prosecutor Laure Beccuau has asked for international arrest warrants. The state’s cyber-crisis centre counts at least fifteen fires and tens of millions of euros of ruined food from one October night.

stories.headline: MAS opens Singapore’s 500-tonne currency vault to foreign central banks’ gold
stories.dek: Six founding clearing banks are named, among them Deutsche Bank and J.P. Morgan. Trading is due to go live in the first quarter of 2027, with a tax waiver following in April.

stories.kicker: The Macro Desk · An Inflation Report Without Inflation
stories.headline: The BLS published an October CPI with no annual rate at all
stories.dek: Prices rose 0.4 per cent on the month and core 0.3 per cent, both above what Wall Street expected. But October 2025 was never collected, so the Bureau could publish no twelve-month figure at all.

stories.headline: Milton and Borosil sell tiffin carriers without publishing a steel grade
stories.dek: Elephant Box names its grade per product line and sells you the gasket. Thermos in Japan publishes heat retention to the degree; its American namesake publishes neither hours nor grade.

stories.headline: TSMC books record NT$586.9bn October revenue, up 59.7% on the year
stories.dek: The filing of 10 November puts January to October at NT$4.49 trillion, 43.3 per cent ahead of 2025 — and beats the company’s own August record by NT$72bn.

stories.headline: Schiit prices the three-watt Magni 6 at $99
stories.dek: The launch of 30 October undercuts the $119 Magni Unity it replaces, adds half a watt, and carries a three-year warranty — but reviewers question its showcase socket.

stories.headline: Audio-Technica puts the $3,799 cypress ATH-AWX7000 on sale in Tokyo
stories.dek: The 353-gram ATH-AWX7000 reached retail on 6 November and had its Japanese debut at the 42nd Autumn Headphone Festival the next day. Still nobody has measured it.

stories.headline: Nitesh Tiwari’s Ramayana takes $52.4m worldwide but $8.9m in America
stories.dek: Sony opened the film on 1,433 United States screens on 5 November. Eighty-three per cent of the gross came from outside America, against a reported budget of about $430m for this half alone.

stories.kicker: The Family Desk · Chatbots And Feelings
stories.headline: JAMA Pediatrics links emotional chatbot use to doubled distress in 39,761 pupils
stories.dek: The University of Ottawa study, published 1 November, found 21.1 per cent of Ontario pupils in grades four to twelve — mean age 12.8 — had asked an artificial intelligence for emotional support.

stories.headline: Helium prices are pushing divers onto rebreathers, ScubaBoard’s threads show
stories.dek: A single deep wreck dive costs about $500 in open-circuit gas against roughly $30 on a recycling loop. Some 23,000 units have sold in ten years, and Asia is the worst-supplied region on earth.

stories.headline: Danny Green’s T-REx trial kept 1.09kg of lean mass on lifters
stories.dek: Nature Medicine published the 120-person, 40-week randomised trial on 9 November. Both groups lost about 22kg; strength rose around a tenth with training and fell around a tenth without it.

stories.kicker: The Diary · Two Deadlines In A Fortnight
stories.headline: Gardens by the Bay opens Christmas Wonderland on 27 November, still unpriced
stories.dek: ART SG’s early-bird offer ends at 11.59pm on 24 November and halves every adult pass. The Gardens’ own ticket line has read “prices will be released soon” for six issues running.

stories.kicker: The Long Read · Korea’s Managed Benefit
stories.headline: South Korea capped manual therapy at 43,850 won and the money moved elsewhere
stories.dek: Seoul’s health ministry fixed the price on 1 July 2026 and made patients pay 95 per cent of it. By August, claims for a cheap spray-and-stretch substitute had risen 218 per cent, on data released by Representative Kim Yoon.
